q-122861.name: Question 1
q-122861.problem:
Which of the following are partitions of the real interval $[1,8]?$

I. $1<2<4<8$

II. $\{1,3,4,8\}$

III. $\{2,4,8\}$
q-122861.worked_solution:
A partition $P$ of a closed interval $[a,b]$ is a finite sequence of real numbers taken from $[a,b]$ such that

$$
a={x}_{0}<{x}_{1}<{x}_{2}<…<{x}_{n}=b\,.
$$

We can express $P$ using set notation as

$$
P=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{n}\}.
$$

 

With that in mind, let's consider each statement:

- Statement I is a partition of $[1,8].$

- Statement II is a partition of $[1,8].$

- Statement III is not a partition of $[1,8]$ since it does not include the left endpoint $a=1.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

q-122979.name: Question 8
q-122979.problem: Let $P=\{{z}_{0},{z}_{1},…,{z}_{q}\}$ be a partition of the interval $[4,9].$ If $Δ{z}_{k}={z}_{k}-{z}_{k-1},$ calculate ${\sum }_{k=1}^{q}7Δ{z}_{k}.$
q-122979.worked_solution:
First, we take the factor $7$ outside the summation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{k=1}^{q}7Δ{z}_{k}=7{\sum }_{k=1}^{q}Δ{z}_{k}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that ${\sum }_{k=1}^{q}Δ{z}_{k}$ is just the length of the interval $[4,9],$ because

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{k=1}^{q}Δ{z}_{k} & =({z}_{1}-{z}_{0})+({z}_{2}-{z}_{1})+({z}_{3}-{z}_{2})+⋯+({z}_{q}-{z}_{q-1}) \\  & =(\cancel{{z}_{1}}-{z}_{0})+(\cancel{{z}_{2}}-\cancel{{z}_{1}})+(\cancel{{z}_{3}}-\cancel{{z}_{2}})+⋯+({z}_{q}-\cancel{{z}_{q-1}}) \\  & =-{z}_{0}+{z}_{q} \\  & ={z}_{q}-{z}_{0} \\  & =9-4 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$

$$

Note that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}$ is just the length of the interval $[2,10],$ because

$$

Therefore,

$$
-4{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}=(-4)\cdot 8=-32.
$$

Let P={z0,z1,…,zq} be a partition of the interval [2,6]. If Δzk=zk−zk−1, calculate ∑k=1q(zk+zk−1)2Δzk.

a
24
b
20
c
16
d
12
e
18
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the constant multiple rule, we can write the summation as

∑k=1q(zk+zk−1)2Δzk=12∑k=1q(zk+zk−1)Δzk.

We can simplify the summation as follows:

∑k=1q(zk+zk−1)Δzk=(z1+z0)Δz1+(z2+z1)Δz2+⋯+(zq+zq−1)Δzn=(z1+z0)(z1−z0)+(z2+z1)(z2−z1)+⋯+(zq+zq−1)(zq−zq−1)=(z12−z02)+(z22−z12)+⋯+(zq2−zq−12)=(z12−z02)+(z22−z12)+⋯+(zq2−zq−12)=−z02+zq2=zq2−z02

Now, since z0=2 and zq=6 are the endpoints of our partition, we have

∑k=1q(zk+zk−1)Δzk=zq2−z02=62−22=32.

Finally, we have

12∑k=1q(zk+zk−1)Δzk=12⋅32=16.
